tier_reason: First-party benchmark with public code (bench/, make bench), zig 0.14.0-dev ReleaseFast and rustc 1.77.2/Criterion stated, but hardware is only a Google Cloud c4-standard-16 instance with no CPU model, so not A; no independent measurement.

corrections.claimed_speedup: 100M-node tree sum (bench/README.md SVGs): Zig sequential baseline 3.63 ns/node, Spice 3.93 ns at 1 thread (sub-ns overhead), 0.36 ns at 16 threads (~11x); Rust sequential baseline 7.48 ns/node, Rayon 22.99 ns at 1 thread (~15 ns overhead), 1.64 ns at 16 threads (~14x). Spice at 16 threads is ~4.6x faster than Rayon in absolute per-node time (derived from page data), but the languages' baselines differ 2x. 1000-node tree: Rayon becomes ~60x slower than its baseline at 32 threads on 16 vCPUs, while Spice stays flat because no work is distributed.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Zig 0.14.0-dev.564+75cf7fca9, ReleaseFast; Rayon side rustc 1.77.2 / cargo 1.77.1 with Criterion
corrections.hardware: Google Cloud c4-standard-16 (16 vCPUs, 60 GB), europe-west4, NixOS 24.05, Linux 6.6.41; CPU model not stated
corrections.caveats: Cross-language comparison: the Zig sequential baseline (3.63 ns/node) is twice as fast as the Rust one (7.48 ns/node), so absolute Spice-vs-Rayon times mix scheduler and codegen differences; the author compares each against its own language's baseline. Rayon scales better (14x vs 11x at 16 threads); Spice's win is sub-nanosecond fork/join overhead and no slowdown on tiny inputs. Single workload (tree sum), single run of make bench, August 2024. Author calls it a research project with minimal tests. Zig, usable from C++ only via a C ABI wrapper.

notes: Record mislabelled 7.48 ns as the sequential baseline; that is Rust's, Zig's is 3.63 ns. Claim corrected with the per-thread numbers read from the bench SVG text; tier stays C, verdict downgrade for the overstated/misattributed claim only. Metadata (0BSD, 973 stars, last commit 2026-03-22) checked.

tier_reason: Benchmark code for staccato, tbb, cilk, openmp and sequential is public in benchmarks/ (run.sh), with g++ 7.2.1 -O3 stated, but the CPU is given only as 'two Intel Xeon E5 v4, 14 cores each' without a model number, so not A; first-party only.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Numbers only in README charts (docs/final.dat-*.png, execution time in us on a natural-log axis): at 56 threads fib(42) Staccato ~14.03 vs Cilk Plus ~14.48 vs TBB ~14.92 log-us, about 1.6x faster than Cilk and 2.4x faster than TBB; dfs 9^9 Staccato ~13.38 vs Cilk ~14.3 vs TBB ~14.6, about 2.5x and 3.4x (derived from page data, chart-read, approximate). Staccato is faster at every thread count on fib/dfs; README says memory-bound matmul/blkmul are almost unaffected.
corrections.caveats: Old baselines (TBB 4.3, Intel Cilk Plus 7.3, both superseded/deprecated). Numbers are read from PNG charts, no text table; ratios assume the log axis is natural log (consistent with fib(42) sequential ~1.4 s). Requires declaring max subtasks per task up front. CPU model not stated beyond Xeon E5 v4. Last commit 2018-06-13.

notes: Charts were readable via raw.githubusercontent.com; approximate ratios added and marked derived. benchmarks/ also has an openmp variant not shown in the charts.

tier_reason: First-party README table from the project's CI bench job (bench/ code public) on a 4-vCPU GitHub runner; no compiler, flags or CPU model, baselines are its own mutex-queue pool, serial code and std::sort.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Best of 5 on a 4-vCPU GitHub runner: fib(36) cutoff 20 serial 28.5 ms, central queue 19.2 ms, stealpool 14.1 ms (2.02x vs serial, ~1.36x vs central queue derived from page data); unbalanced tree 90.6 / 25.7 / 23.4 ms (3.86x vs serial); 1M empty tasks central queue 526.2 ms vs stealpool 145.9 ms (3.6x); reduce 16M doubles 165.8 vs 56.4 ms (2.94x vs serial); parallel quicksort 20M ints 589 ms vs 1507 ms for std::sort.
corrections.baseline: self-written central-queue thread pool (std::deque behind a mutex), serial code, and std::sort (not TBB/OpenMP/Rayon)
corrections.caveats: Baselines are a strawman mutex-queue pool, serial code and single-threaded std::sort; no comparison with TBB, OpenMP or Rayon. Noisy shared CI runner, compiler/flags not stated, std library not stated. No license file, so reference only. 0 stars, 6 commits; low-confidence data point.

notes: Record's '2.02x fib over central queue' was wrong: 2.02x is vs serial; vs central queue it is ~1.36x. Tier unchanged at C; downgrade for the misattributed claim. No LICENSE file found (LICENSE, LICENSE.md, LICENSE.txt all 404).
